description:
pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:956-974 (`build_first_valid_path`) and lib.rs:987-1048 (`build_first_valid_path_with_config`). The rustdoc covers when to use it, what errors it returns, and what's out of scope (async, caching, promoting build_path) — but does **not** characterize the worst-case work the helper performs per call.

The complexity contract callers need is:

- **Candidate iteration**: bounded by `PathBuilderConfig::dfs_budget` (default DEFAULT_DFS_BUDGET = 10_000). This is the hard cap on DFS frame entries; the helper inherits it from the underlying `PathCandidates` iterator.
- **Per-candidate `pkix_path::validate_path` cost**: unbounded by this crate. Each yielded chain is independently fed through `validate_path`, which runs the full RFC 5280 §6.1 state machine plus signature verification per intermediate.
- **Worst case under defaults**: roughly `O(dfs_budget * chain_length * signature_verification_cost)`. With default `max_depth = 10`, that's up to ~10,000 candidates × ~10-cert chains × per-cert signature work. In adversarial cross-signed pools where many candidates differ only in deep intermediate selection, this can be substantial wall-clock — far more than callers extrapolate from `build_path`'s single-shot cost.

Callers in latency-sensitive paths (TLS handshake, OCSP responder, on-line signing services) need this number to make informed timeout decisions. The current doc gives them no signal — they have to read the source to discover the iterator-driven retry loop.

Specifically called out:

- The "Out of scope" section says async / parallel evaluation is not supported. Good. But that's a feature-scope statement, not a complexity bound — it tells the caller "you can't make this faster," not "here's how slow it can get."
- The relationship table says `build_first_valid_path` returns "First candidate that passes `validate_path`" — accurate, but the cost of "first that passes" depends on how many fail first.

Required additions to the rustdoc:

1. Explicit complexity section: "Worst-case work per call: O(dfs_budget) DFS frame entries × O(per-candidate validate_path cost). Per-candidate cost is `pkix_path::validate_path`'s responsibility; this crate bounds candidate count but not per-candidate work."

2. Cross-link to `PathBuilderConfig::dfs_budget` so callers tightening the iteration bound see the helper as the consumer.

3. Note that callers wanting a per-call wall-clock bound should drop down to `build_path_candidates` and limit the iteration count themselves (the doc on `PathCandidates` already suggests this for the case "want to limit the number of candidates tried"; the cross-link from `build_first_valid_path` is missing).

The undocumented complexity is a real footgun for callers who model `build_first_valid_path` as a thin wrapper over `build_path`.
title: build_first_valid_path time-complexity contract not documented; per-candidate validate_path cost unbounded by crate
